contract: Pure consent record over a caller-held state: request/3 opens, keeps or supersedes (revision + 1) a request bound structurally to the ASK action, escrow, policy identity and requirement; release/4 accepts host-verified evidence or a retained run/root consent, runs gates 0-21 in Cure (run, request, verifier allowlist, revocation, consumption, binding-only reuse, decision, Unix-ms issue/age/expiry, scope, approver, self-approval, re-decide, DENY, policy, payload, requirement, approver authority) and emits only the current decision's escrow within approver authority, once. select_retained/3, revalidate/3, revoke/2, apply_event/2 and replay/1 complete the Contract; replay returns state only.
limits: No authentication, verifier transport, durable storage, shared Run schema, UI prompting, security certification or identity guarantee; trusted fixtures stand in for verifier output.
Laws are in decision-split (hypothesis) form; self-approval, rejection and released-twice laws cover fresh evidence; retained paths are covered by the general laws and tests.

Test-grounded only: lookup after insert (release-then-release), replay and request/3 idempotence, eq_value reflexivity and Elixir agreement, released writes equal to the originally bound escrow, retained selection order, time/age comparisons (native <=, < and + are neutral in pinned Cure), the Elixir-side validation and control-key refusal.
Check 7 (consumed) is defence in depth: public transitions consume a once key only together with its release record, so check 2 or 4 reports first.
Single approver per request; evidence scope must equal the requirement scope; exact-value authority. Changing these needs a new Piece ID.
A fixed retained choice can block other valid consents when the chosen reviewer lost authority; the owner revokes that consent or obtains fresh evidence.
Volatile pure value: the owner serializes transitions, retains events durably if needed, and owns dispatch of released writes; a timeout after dispatch is an unknown outcome.

grounding.claim: For all state, key, source, context: if approved(release_check(...)) = False then release emits no writes.
Same hypothesis: release returns the input state unchanged.
For all gate lists p, s, gate g with blocks(g) = True and any final check: run_gates(p ++ [g | s], final) is not approved (induction on p).
For all inputs: subset(writes_of(release(...)), approver authority) = True, with respect to eq_write.
For all inputs: released writes are a subset of the context's own authority (from escrowed_within_own), with respect to eq_write.
For every context whose parent authority is p (with_parent(ctx, p)): released writes are a subset of p, with respect to eq_write.
If the current Cure decide verdict is Deny, release emits no writes, whatever the gates returned (hypothesis form).
If eq_ints(run id, key run) = False, release emits no writes, for fresh and retained sources (hypothesis form).
For fresh evidence: if has_release(releases, key) = True, release emits no writes (hypothesis form).
For fresh evidence with decision Reject (any other fields): release emits no writes.
For fresh evidence: if eq_ints(reviewer, trusted proposer) = True, release emits no writes (hypothesis form).

Pinned Cure checks the production release with a clean audit; every function is @total; Auth types are module-qualified. Tests reject a refused release that emits writes, a release without the approver guard, a passing self-approval gate and an unfinished law.

Listed scenarios: payload/policy/hash drift, release DENY, stale revision and supersession, self-approval and forged proposer, under-authorized approver, model text, verifier allowlist, age/expiry boundaries, revocation, once/run/root scope, retained selection (two reviewers, stale earliest, T1, T2, byte-order tie), revalidate, replay, restore, bounds, pinned refusal order. Not universal proofs.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler, kernel and audit.
Relies on pinned Elixir/OTP term equality and binary handling.

Only the trusted host's configured verifier path builds evidence; the owner supplies a trusted Unix-ms clock, Run/root/ancestry, proposer identity, effect class and current authorities, and serializes transitions.

telemetry.contract: Pure; the owning Unit/Assembly instruments. Release records and events are caller-retained records, not telemetry.

config.contract: Per call, no default, no hot reconfiguration: verifiers (1..64 identity texts, exact match), max_age (integer ms, 1..2^63-1, compared as now - issued_at < max_age) and the current policy for re-decide.

control.contract: No lifecycle; revocation is a domain transition on the caller's state, not a Control.
